articles.title: Finding Why SYSVOL on FRS Blocks a New Domain Controller
articles.excerpt: This post first appeared on the ET Ducky blog. I build ET Ducky, an RMM that reads ETW on Windows and eBPF on Linux. A new Windows Server 2019 or later server can't be promoted to a domain controller…
articles.body: This post first appeared on the ET Ducky blog. I build ET Ducky, an RMM that reads ETW on Windows and eBPF on Linux. A new Windows Server 2019 or later server can't be promoted to a domain controller in a domain that still replicates SYSVOL with the File Replication Service (FRS). Promotion stops at the prerequisite check with "The specified domain contoso.com is still using the File Replication Service (FRS) to replicate the SYSVOL share." The message also says "You MUST migrate the specified domain to use DFS Replication using the DFSRMIG command before continuing." This post covers how to confirm which service replicates SYSVOL, check replication health, move the domain through the dfsrmig states, and clear the two blockers Microsoft documents for the migration.

articles.title: RAG-Fusion with Lightweight Python Implementation
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: This article explains RAG-Fusion, a method to improve Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by generating multiple search queries and fusing their results. It highlights a lightweight Python imp…
articles.body: TL;DR: This article explains RAG-Fusion, a method to improve Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by generating multiple search queries and fusing their results. It highlights a lightweight Python implementation by Rodrigo Arenas that uses BM25 and Reciprocal Rank Fusion without external dependencies. Ever struggled with a RAG system that just doesn't quite hit the mark, returning vaguely related documents instead of direct answers? It often comes down to the initial retrieval step. A single, static search query, even with vector embeddings, can easily miss the full intent of a complex or ambiguous user question, leading to incomplete or inaccurate LLM responses. This is where RAG-Fusion steps in to refine your retrieval strategy.

articles.title: Modeling a seven-working-day setup as a state machine of owned steps

articles.body: A new trade business needs its tools to arrive as a coherent system, not as a collection of disconnected tasks. At Neuron Expert, the setup covers the owner’s own CRM, website, business phone number with an AI receptionist, and listings. We model that setup as an ordered state machine: every piece of work has an owner, a visible status, timestamps, and a record of hands-on time. The problem is not a checklist A checklist can say that a website exists or that a profile is pending. It cannot answer the operational questions that arise during setup: Which step is currently blocking the next one? Is the next action with an automated session, a browser agent, the client, or Neuron’s owner? Has work started but not finished? Is a delay caused by client verification rather than internal work?

articles.title: Which Is the Best Game Engine: Unity, Unreal, or Godot?
articles.excerpt: Originally published at simulatedsphere.com. There is no universal "best" game engine. There is a best engine for a specific production shape: a two-person mobile team, a 20-person systems-heavy indie…
articles.body: Originally published at simulatedsphere.com . There is no universal "best" game engine . There is a best engine for a specific production shape: a two-person mobile team, a 20-person systems-heavy indie, a cinematic console team, a classroom, or a studio building a toolchain it expects to maintain for a decade. Unity , Unreal , and Godot can all ship real games. The difference is not whether they are "capable." The difference is where each engine spends your budget: on rendering quality, iteration speed, tooling maturity, licensing risk, source control friction, runtime footprint, hiring, and escape hatches when the editor fights you. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. So, I picked out the ten time travel movies you need to own, from classic blockbusters like Back to the Future, through to modern gems such as Needle in a Timestack, where the only obstacle to time travel is your bank balance. We do mean own, too. All too often, we've sat down to rewatch a film to find it's vanished from our streaming service. At best, it's rematerialized on a different streaming service; at worst, it's been exterminated as some media conglomerate's tax write-off. Even 'buying' a movie, you're just getting a license that can be revoked at any time. The solution?
